mainTopic: The cancelled gift of a mistaken שכיב מרע, the Torah sources for מתנת שכיב מרע, and weather signs for the year
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא about a dying man who gave away his property because he thought he had no son, or that his wife was not pregnant. If it turns out he does have an heir, the gift is cancelled. Even the רבנן agree, because he said 'דומה' and so stated his reason out loud. The גמרא then asks for the source showing that מתנת שכיב מרע works מן התורה without a קנין. רב learns it from 'והעברתם' and רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה learns it from 'ונתתם'. The גמרא explains why each one rejects the other's word. Two more sources come from the פסוקים about חזקיהו and אחיתופל, who gave instructions to their households before dying. This leads to אחיתופל's three instructions to his sons. That opens a discussion of weather signs: a clear שבועות, the smoke on the מזבח at the end of סוכות, and which winds help which crops. The גמרא settles a contradiction by saying one source describes בבל and the other ארץ ישראל. The amud ends with רב זביד's sign about the first day of ראש השנה and a question about its practical use.

steps.title: A dying man's gift is cancelled if he wrongly thought he had no heir
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with two cases: a שכיב מרע says 'I thought I had a son' or 'I thought my wife was pregnant,' and now gives his property to someone else. If he really has a son or a pregnant wife, the gift is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I thought I had a son. Now that I have no son, my property goes to so-and-so.' Or he was sick in bed and they asked him, 'Who gets your property?' He said, 'I thought my wife was pregnant. Now that she is not pregnant, my property goes to so-and-so.' If it then becomes known that he has a son, or that his wife was pregnant, his gift is not a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that began at the end of the previous daf. It rules that the gift is void if the man really does have an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the man himself ties the gift to the belief that he has no heir. When that belief turns out to be wrong, the gift falls away. The next steps examine whose view this ruling follows.

keyTerms.meaning: His gift is not a valid gift

phrases.english: I thought that I had a son,
now that I do not have a son –
my property goes to so-and-so;
if he was sick and lying in bed,
and they said to him: to whom does his property go?
he said to them: I thought that my wife was pregnant,
now that my wife is not pregnant –
my property goes to so-and-so;
and it became known that he has a son
or that his wife was pregnant –
his gift is not a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שכיב מרע who gave his property away because he believed he had no son, or no pregnant wife, loses the gift if it turns out he does have an heir.

steps.title: Does this follow only רבי שמעון בן מנסיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and not the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, and not the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that this ruling fits only one side of an earlier מחלוקת. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous daf, רבי שמעון בן מנסיא held that we cancel a gift when we can assume the giver would not have given it had he known the truth. The רבנן did not cancel the gift in that case. Since this ברייתא cancels the gift, it seems to follow only רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who cancels a gift based on the giver's mistaken belief

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Shall we say it is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא,
and not the רבנן?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which side of the earlier מחלוקת the ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא can fit the רבנן or only רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree when he said 'I thought'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even the רבנן agree here, because the man openly said 'דומה,' explaining why he gave the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. When he says 'I thought,' it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can follow everyone. Saying 'I thought' makes this case different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case the רבנן would not guess at what the giver was thinking. Here the giver himself said his reason out loud, so even the רבנן agree the gift depends on that reason.
steps.whatToRemember: A gift is cancelled by everyone's opinion when the giver openly states the mistaken reason he is giving it.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the רבנן,
'I thought' is different.
phrases.notes: He means: once the man said 'I thought,' he showed that this was his reason for giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא fits only רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the man stated his reason ('דומה'), even the רבנן agree the gift is void.

steps.title: Why did anyone even ask?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier question was raised at all, since the difference seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own earlier question. If 'I thought' is clearly different, why suggest it only follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 seems so plain that the question in step 2 looks unnecessary. This sets up an explanation of what the asker was thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks it / raises the question

phrases.english: And the one who asks it –
why does he ask it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since 'דומה' plainly shows his reason, there was no reason to think the ברייתא follows only רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: He might only be expressing his sorrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that one could have thought the man mentioned his son only out of sadness, not as the reason for the gift. The ברייתא teaches that it really is his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that he is only mentioning his sorrow. It teaches us that it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question made sense. Mentioning the son could have been just an expression of grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'I thought I had a son' were only a sad remark, it would not be a stated condition, and the case would depend on guessing his intent, like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. The ברייתא teaches that these words count as his reason, so the gift is cancelled even according to the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Words like 'I thought I had a son' are treated as the giver's real reason, not just a sad remark.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is his sorrow that he is mentioning,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the hidden assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His mention of the son is only an expression of grief, not a condition of the gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mention of the son is the stated reason for the gift, so the gift is void if a son exists.

steps.title: Where does the Torah teach the gift of a dying man?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רב asks for the Torah source showing that a מתנת שכיב מרע works מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that the gift of a dying man is from the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב asks for a Torah source for the special power of a dying man's gift, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person's gift needs a formal קנין, but a שכיב מרע's spoken words are enough. רב wants to show that this rule comes from the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The gift of a person on his deathbed

phrases.english: רבי זירא said in the name of רב:
From where do we know regarding the gift of a dying man
that it is from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מִנַּיִן לְמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the Torah basis for מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that a dying man's gift is valid by Torah law.

steps.title: The word 'והעברתם' hints at the dying man's gift
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from 'והעברתם את נחלתו לבתו' that there is another kind of 'passing over' of property like ירושה, and that is מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'You shall pass his inheritance to his daughter.' There is another kind of passing over that is like this one. Which is it? The gift of a dying man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers his question with a פסוק about inheritance. The word 'והעברתם' points to another transfer that works like ירושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושה passes to the heirs without any קנין. The extra word 'והעברתם' teaches that another transfer works the same way, and that is the gift of a שכיב מרע, which also needs no formal קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall cause to pass over

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, מתנת שכיב מרע is from the Torah and works like ירושה, learned from the word 'והעברתם.'
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is about a daughter inheriting. רב is not learning the daughter's law here; he is learning from the word 'והעברתם' that another transfer, the dying man's gift, works like ירושה.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'You shall cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter' –
you have another case of passing over
that is like this one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵי זוֹ? זוֹ מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע.
phrases.english: And which is it? This is the gift of a dying man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'והעברתם' teaches another transfer like ירושה, which is מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a Torah basis for why a dying man's spoken words can transfer property without a קנין.

steps.title: A second source: 'And you shall give'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה learns מתנת שכיב מרע from the word 'ונתתם' in the inheritance verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: we learn it from here: 'And you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.' This teaches that there is another kind of 'giving' that is like this one. Which is it? That is the gift of a שכיב מרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different answer to רב's question from step 6. It uses a different word in the same section of the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance passes to the heirs on its own, so the Torah did not need to say 'you shall give.' רב נחמן reads the extra word 'giving' as hinting to another transfer that works like inheritance, which is מתנת שכיב מרע. It is the same idea as רב's answer, built on a different word.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift given by a dangerously ill person

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said: from here:
"And you shall give his inheritance to his brothers"

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ נְתִינָה אַחֶרֶת שֶׁהִיא כָּזוֹ.
phrases.english: you have another kind of giving that is like this one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵי זוֹ? זוֹ מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע.
phrases.english: And which is it? This is the gift of a dying person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second Torah source, different from רב's 'והעברתם'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for מתנת שכיב מרע (from step 6).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'ונתתם': there is another 'giving' like inheritance, which is מתנת שכיב מרע.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב נחמן use 'והעברתם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן did not learn the law from 'והעברתם' the way רב did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן, what is his reason that he did not learn it from 'And you shall pass over'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן picked a different word instead of using רב's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's derivation from 'והעברתם' looks good, so why not accept it? The גמרא assumes רב נחמן must need that word for something else.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman, what is the reason
that he did not say it from "and you shall pass over"?
phrases.notes: This is רב's source from step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רב נחמן chose a different source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'והעברתם' already teaches the law, there seems to be no reason to look for another word.

steps.title: רב נחמן needs 'והעברתם' for רבי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן uses 'והעברתם' for רבי's teaching that only a daughter's inheritance can move from one tribe to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word for רבי's teaching, as it was taught: רבי says: with all the other heirs the Torah says 'giving,' but here it says 'passing over.' No heir moves an inheritance from tribe to tribe except a daughter, because her son and her husband inherit from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'והעברתם' is already used for a different lesson, so רב נחמן cannot use it for מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי notices that only by the daughter does the Torah switch from 'giving' to 'passing over.' A daughter's son and husband may come from another tribe, so her inheritance can 'pass over' to a new tribe. Since the word is busy with this lesson, רב נחמן learns מתנת שכיב מרע from 'ונתתם' instead.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, not רבי זירא. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: He needs that word for the teaching of Rabbi,
as it was taught: Rabbi says:
With all of them, "giving" is said,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the other heirs in that section: brothers, uncles, relatives.

phrases.english: and here "passing over" is said;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִשֵּׁבֶט לְשֵׁבֶט,
phrases.english: there is no one who moves an inheritance from tribe to tribe,
except a daughter,
since her son and her husband inherit from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'והעברתם' is free to teach מתנת שכיב מרע, so רב נחמן should have used it.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והעברתם' teaches רבי's lesson about a daughter moving property between tribes, so רב נחמן uses 'ונתתם'.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי זירא use 'ונתתם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the other way: why didn't רבי זירא learn the law from 'ונתתם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא, what is his reason that he did not learn it from 'And you shall give'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around and asks why רבי זירא (in the name of רב) did not use רב נחמן's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ונתתם' is an extra word that hints to another giving, רבי זירא could have used it too. The גמרא wants to know why he passed it over.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira, what is the reason
that he did not say it from "and you shall give"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same kind of question as step 9, now aimed at the other side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ונתתם' seems to be an available hint, so why not use it?

steps.title: 'ונתתם' is just the Torah's normal way of speaking
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא holds that 'giving' is the ordinary way the verse talks, so nothing extra can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is just the normal way the verse speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי זירא the word 'ונתתם' is not extra. It is simply how the Torah usually says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן saw 'giving' as an unneeded word and learned from it. רבי זירא says the Torah uses 'giving' for all the heirs as its regular style, so it carries no hint. Only the unusual word 'והעברתם' can teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way the verse speaks

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that מתנת שכיב מרע works מן התורה. They only disagree about which word in the verse is the extra one we can learn from.

phrases.english: That is the usual way of the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is normal style, not an extra word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ונתתם' is extra and can teach מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ונתתם' is ordinary Torah wording, so רבי זירא learns only from 'והעברתם'.

steps.title: A third source: 'Give instructions to your household'
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר ירמיה learns מתנת שכיב מרע from ישעיהו telling the dying חזקיהו 'צו לביתך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר ירמיה said: we learn it from here: 'In those days חזקיהו became deathly ill, and ישעיהו בן אמוץ the prophet came to him and said: So says ה׳: give instructions to your household, for you will die and not live.' This shows it works through instructions alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer to the question of step 6, this time from a verse in נביאים instead of the inheritance verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו tells a dying man to 'instruct' his household. This shows that a dying person's words alone, without any formal act of transfer, are enough to pass on his property.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three sources for מתנת שכיב מרע: 'והעברתם' (רב), 'ונתתם' (רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה), and 'צו לביתך' (רב מנשיא בר ירמיה). The next step adds a fourth. All of them teach that a dying person's gift works through words alone.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya said: from here:
"In those days Hezekiah became deathly ill,"

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹא אֵלָיו יְשַׁעְיָהוּ בֶן אָמוֹץ הַנָּבִיא,
phrases.english: "and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him,"
"and said to him: So says the Lord,"
"give instructions to your household,"
"for you will die and you will not live"
by a mere instruction.
phrases.notes: He means the dying man's spoken instructions alone are enough to transfer his property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third source, separate from both inheritance-verse derivations.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for מתנת שכיב מרע (from step 6).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'צו לביתך': a dying person transfers property through instructions alone.

steps.title: Learning the dying man's gift from אחיתופל
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל learns מתנת שכיב מרע from the verse saying that אחיתופל 'commanded his household' before he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל said: we learn it from here: 'And אחיתופל saw that his advice was not followed, and he saddled his donkey, went home to his city, commanded his household, and strangled himself.' This shows that a plain instruction is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more answer to the question of where מתנת שכיב מרע comes from. רמי בר יחזקאל uses the story of אחיתופל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחיתופל was about to die, and the verse says he 'commanded' his household. Since the verse treats his instructions as meaningful, it shows that a dying person's spoken words alone can give away his property, with no formal קנין. This is a different verse from the one רב מנשיא בר ירמיה used in step 13, but it proves the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's advisor, who joined אבשלום's rebellion
with a mere instruction, just words

steps.whatToRemember: We have now seen several sources for מתנת שכיב מרע. All of them show that a dying person's spoken instructions take effect even without a קנין.

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel said: from here:
"And Achitofel saw that his advice was not followed,
and he saddled the donkey,
and went to his house, to his city,
and he commanded his household, and strangled himself":
with a mere instruction.
phrases.notes: In other words, his words alone were enough. No formal act of acquiring was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different verse for the same rule that רב מנשיא בר ירמיה learned from חזקיהו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מתנת שכיב מרע is learned from אחיתופל commanding his household before his death.

steps.title: אחיתופל's three instructions to his sons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the three things אחיתופל told his sons: avoid disputes, don't rebel against בית דוד, and sow wheat if שבועות is a clear day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: אחיתופל commanded his sons three things. Do not get involved in disputes. Do not rebel against the kingship of בית דוד. And if the day of שבועות is clear, sow wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just mentioned אחיתופל's 'commands', it brings a ברייתא that tells us what those commands actually were. This is a side topic, not part of the legal discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two instructions are lessons he learned from his own downfall, since he took part in אבשלום's rebellion. The third is practical farming advice: the weather on שבועות tells you whether wheat will do well that year. The next steps discuss this third instruction.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה אֲחִיתוֹפֶל אֶת בָּנָיו –
phrases.english: Achitofel commanded his sons three things:
Do not be involved in a dispute,
and do not rebel against the kingship of the house of David,
and if the festival of Atzeret is clear,
sow wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה אֲחִיתוֹפֶל אֶת בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up on the word 'commanded' in the verse about אחיתופל and tells us what he commanded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחיתופל told his sons to avoid disputes, not to rebel against בית דוד, and to sow wheat if שבועות is clear.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the sign is a cloudy day
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the correct wording of the ברייתא is 'cloudy', not 'clear'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: what was actually said is 'cloudy'.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא corrects the wording of אחיתופל's third instruction. He says wheat will do well if שבועות is cloudy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of the ברייתא's version. Now we have two sides, 'clear' and 'cloudy', and that sets up the next step, which explains how both can be right.

keyTerms.meaning: it was said, this was the wording

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
"Cloudy" was what was said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different wording of the ברייתא's third instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sign for sowing wheat is a cloudy שבועות, not a clear one.

steps.title: The נהרדעי: a north wind is what counts
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי, in the name of רבי יעקב, explain that neither word is meant literally. A cloudy day with a north wind blowing counts as 'clear'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of נהרדעא said in the name of רבי יעקב: 'clear' doesn't mean completely clear, and 'cloudy' doesn't mean completely cloudy. Even if it is cloudy, as long as a north wind is blowing the clouds, that counts as 'clear'.
steps.whatsHappening: The נהרדעי settle the argument between 'clear' and 'cloudy'. They explain that both versions describe the same kind of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good sign is a day that has clouds but also has a north wind blowing them. You could call that day 'cloudy' because of the clouds, or 'clear' because the wind keeps them moving. So the two wordings don't really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages of the city of נהרדעא

phrases.english: The people of Nehardea say in the name of Rabbi Yaakov:
"Clear" does not mean actually clear,
and "cloudy" does not mean actually cloudy;
rather, even if it is cloudy
and a north wind is blowing it,
that is "clear."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement over wording between the ברייתא and מר זוטרא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining terms so that both versions describe the same day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Clear' and 'cloudy' seem to be opposite signs.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cloudy day with a north wind blowing counts as 'clear', so both versions agree.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the smoke on the מזבח at the end of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רב אשי that they connect the north-wind idea to רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching about watching which way the smoke of the מזבח leaned at the end of סוכות. Smoke leaning north meant heavy rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: we teach this on the statement of רב יצחק בר אבדימי. He said: at the end of the last day of סוכות, everyone watched the smoke from the fire on the מזבח. If it leaned north, the poor were happy and the householders were sad, because the year's rains would be heavy and the produce would rot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא says the idea about the north wind is taught in a different setting, with רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching about smoke at the end of סוכות. The גמרא then begins quoting that teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of סוכות people looked at which way the wind blew the smoke on the מזבח, and they read it as a sign for the year's rain. Smoke leaning north means a south wind, which brings lots of rain. That means plenty of food that does not store well and must be sold cheaply. This helps the poor and hurts the owners.

keyTerms.meaning: we teach it, we attach this teaching to

keyTerms.term: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
keyTerms.meaning: the end of the last day of סוכות
the smoke of the woodpile on the מזבח
householders, landowners who have produce to sell

steps.confusionAlert: The smoke leans the opposite way from where the wind comes from. Smoke leaning north means a south wind is blowing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן – אַדְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ,
phrases.english: We teach it on the statement of Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the teaching about the north wind as a sign for the crops.

phrases.english: as Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג,
phrases.english: At the end of the last festival day of the Chag,
everyone would look at the smoke of the woodpile;
phrases.notes: This is the fire burning on the מזבח.

phrases.english: if it leaned toward the north,
the poor were happy and the householders were sad,
because the year's rains would be plentiful,
and produce would rot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנַן אַדְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the north-wind idea in a different setting, the smoke at the end of סוכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the smoke leaned north at the end of סוכות, the year would be rainy and produce would rot. This is good for the poor and bad for householders.

steps.title: What the other directions of the smoke meant
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching continues. Smoke leaning south meant little rain and produce that keeps. Smoke leaning east meant everyone was happy. Smoke leaning west meant everyone was sad.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the smoke leaned south, the poor were sad and the householders were happy, because there would be little rain and the produce would keep. If it leaned east, everyone was happy. If it leaned west, everyone was sad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רב יצחק בר אבדימי. It goes through the other three directions the smoke could lean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoke leaning south means a north wind, the same north wind from step 17. It brings little rain, so food is scarce but keeps well, which helps the owners. The text gives no reasons for east and west. It only says that east was good for everyone and west was bad for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: keep well, stay fresh in storage

steps.whatToRemember: The smoke on the מזבח at the end of סוכות was read as a sign for the year's rain. North meant heavy rain, south meant light rain, east was good for everyone, and west was bad for everyone.

phrases.english: If it leaned toward the south,
phrases.notes: Smoke goes south when a north wind is blowing, the same north wind from step 17.

phrases.english: the poor were sad and the householders were happy,
because the year's rains would be few,
and produce would keep.
If it leaned toward the east, everyone was happy.
Toward the west, everyone was sad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of directions in רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: South meant little rain and produce that keeps (good for owners), east was good for everyone, and west was bad for everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא about winds seems to contradict the smoke teaching
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the east wind is always good and the west wind is always bad. This seems to clash with רב יצחק בר אבדימי's smoke signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a ברייתא: An east wind is always good. A west wind is always bad. A north wind is good for wheat once it has grown a third, and bad for olives when they are blossoming. A south wind is bad for wheat once it has grown a third, and good for olives when they are blossoming.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about which winds help or hurt crops. It brings it to challenge רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching from the previous steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, smoke leaning east meant everyone was happy and smoke leaning west meant everyone was sad. Smoke is pushed away from the side the wind blows from, so smoke leaning east means a west wind was blowing. That makes the west wind the happy sign, but this ברייתא says the west wind is always bad and the east wind is always good.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other: the גמרא is pointing out a contradiction between two sources
One third. Here it means a third of the grain's growth
Blossom, as when olive trees are flowering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which way the smoke leans with where the wind comes from. Smoke leaning east was pushed by a wind blowing from the west.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: This sets the ברייתא against רב יצחק בר אבדימי's smoke signs from just before.

phrases.english: An east wind is always good.
A west wind is always harmful.
A north wind is good for wheat
once it has reached a third of its growth,
and harmful to olives when they are blossoming.
And a south wind is harmful to wheat
once it has reached a third of its growth,
and good for olives when they are blossoming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the east and west smoke signs from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching that smoke leaning east, meaning a west wind, made everyone happy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the west wind always harmful and the east wind always good, which is the opposite of the smoke signs.

steps.title: A memory aid: the שולחן in the north and the מנורה in the south
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, or some say מר זוטרא or רב נחמן בר יצחק, gives a memory aid for the ברייתא. The שולחן is in the north and the מנורה is in the south, and each one 'increases its own.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said, and some say it was מר זוטרא, and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק: Here is your memory aid. The שולחן is in the north and the מנורה is in the south. This one increases its own, and that one increases its own.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a simple way to remember which wind helps which crop in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שולחן holds bread made from wheat, and it stands in the north, so the north wind helps wheat. The מנורה is lit with olive oil, and it stands in the south, so the south wind helps olives. This helps the reader remember the ברייתא. The contradiction from Step 20 is answered in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: the same teaching is said in someone else's name
The Table in the בית המקדש that held the לחם הפנים
The Menorah in the בית המקדש, lit with olive oil
Increases its own: each wind helps the crop that belongs to its side

phrases.english: And רב יוסף said,
and some say it was מר זוטרא,
and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק:
And your memory aid is: the Table is in the north,
and the Menorah is in the south.
This one increases its own,
phrases.notes: The north wind helps the wheat, which was used for the bread on the שולחן.

phrases.english: and that one increases its own!
phrases.notes: The south wind helps the olives, whose oil lit the מנורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְאִיתֵּימָא מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְסִימָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory aid for the north and south wind rules in the ברייתא from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: North wind helps wheat (שולחן, north) and south wind helps olives (מנורה, south).

steps.title: One teaching is for us and the other is for them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי are talking about different places. One is about בבל and the other is about ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 20 by saying the two sources describe different lands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that praises the east wind is about בבל, where 'we' live. There water is plentiful, so a dry east wind does no harm. רב יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching is about ארץ ישראל, where 'they' live. There water is scarce, the dry east wind hurts the crops, and the west wind brings rain.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the standard opening of an answer
This is for us, the people in בבל
That is for them, the people in ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources are true. Which wind helps depends on the land: the east wind is good in בבל, and the west wind is good in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' means the people in בבל, and 'them' means the people in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא לַן, וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction raised in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different places: each source is talking about a different land
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both sources describe the same place, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes בבל and the smoke teaching describes ארץ ישראל, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: אבא שאול: a clear שבועות is a good sign for the year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא שאול: if the day of שבועות is clear, it is a good sign for the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא שאול says: If the festival of שבועות is a clear day, it is a good sign for the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא connected to the weather on שבועות, the same day אחיתופל spoke about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 15, אחיתופל said to sow wheat if שבועות was clear. אבא שאול widens this: a clear שבועות is a good sign for the entire year, not only for the wheat.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught: introduces a ברייתא
The name חז"ל use for the festival of שבועות
Clear, as in a clear-skied day

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Shaul says:
If the festival of Shavuot is clear,
it is a good sign for the entire year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the weather on שבועות from Step 15 after finishing the discussion of winds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clear שבועות is a good sign for the whole year.

steps.title: רב זביד: the first day of ראש השנה shows the year's temperature
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says that if the first day of ראש השנה is warm, the whole year will be warm. If it is cold, the whole year will be cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: This first day of the new year, if it is warm, the whole year will be warm. If it is cold, the whole year will be cold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד adds another weather sign for the coming year, this one based on the first day of ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול used שבועות as a sign of whether the year would be good. רב זביד uses the first day of ראש השנה as a sign of whether the year will be warm or cold.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of the year, ראש השנה

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
This first day of the new year,
if it is warm, the whole year will be warm,
if it is cold, the whole year will be cold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: הַאי יוֹמָא קַמָּא דְּרֵישׁ שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second sign for the coming year, next to אבא שאול's sign from Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The weather on the first day of ראש השנה shows whether the whole year will be warm or cold.

steps.title: What practical difference does this sign make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes to know רב זביד's sign about whether the year will be warm or cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters to know רב זביד's sign. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that the year will be warm or cold does not change the weather. So the גמרא wants to know what someone would actually do differently with this information. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of רב זביד's sign from Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a person gains in practice from knowing whether the coming year will be warm or cold
